\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تشخيص} (tashkhīṣ)}{تشخيص (tashkhīṣ)}]{\ar{تشخيص} (tashkhīṣ) — a diagnosis}

\label{lesson:AR-C510-tashkhis}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a vaccination, then the Arabic for a swelling.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تشخيص}}
\textbf{\ar{تشخيص}} — \emph{tashkhīṣ} — \textquotedblleft{}a diagnosis\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{تشخيص} \ar{الطبيب} \ar{صحيحا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna tashkhīṣ aṭ-ṭabīb ṣaḥīḥan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor's diagnosis was correct.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تشخيص}} (\emph{tashkhīṣ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-kh-ṣ}, \textquotedblleft{}a person, a figure seen from afar\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Shakhṣ, a person, which you know, is from the same root; Form II is to make a thing stand out clearly.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tashkhīṣ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tashkhīṣ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna tashkhīṣ aṭ-ṭabīb ṣaḥīḥan.} — The doctor's diagnosis was correct.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a vaccination, then the Arabic for a swelling, then say \emph{tashkhīṣ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تشخيص} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A diagnosis\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تحليل} (taḥlīl)}{تحليل (taḥlīl)}]{\ar{تحليل} (taḥlīl) — a lab test; an analysis}

\label{lesson:AR-C510-tahlil}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a swelling, then the Arabic for a diagnosis.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تحليل}}
\textbf{\ar{تحليل}} — \emph{taḥlīl} — \textquotedblleft{}a lab test; an analysis\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{طلب} \ar{الطبيب} \ar{تحليل} \ar{دم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṭalaba aṭ-ṭabīb taḥlīl dam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor asked for a blood test.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تحليل}} (\emph{taḥlīl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-l-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to untie, to loosen\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Ḥall, a solution, which you know, is from the same root: taḥlīl takes a thing apart.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥlīl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taḥlīl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭalaba aṭ-ṭabīb taḥlīl dam.} — The doctor asked for a blood test.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a swelling, then the Arabic for a diagnosis, then say \emph{taḥlīl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تحليل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A lab test; an analysis\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أشعة} (ashiʿʿa)}{أشعة (ashiʿʿa)}]{\ar{أشعة} (ashiʿʿa) — X-rays; rays}

\label{lesson:AR-C510-ashia}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a diagnosis, then the Arabic for a lab test.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أشعة}}
\textbf{\ar{أشعة}} — \emph{ashiʿʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}X-rays; rays\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{صور} \ar{الطبيب} \ar{ساقه} \ar{بالأشعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṣawwara aṭ-ṭabīb sāqahu bi-l-ashiʿʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor X-rayed his leg.
\end{quote}

It is the plural of \ar{شعاع}, a ray.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أشعة}} (\emph{ashiʿʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-ʿ-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to spread, to scatter (of light)\textquotedblright{} (Lane). A shuʿāʿ is a ray spreading out from the sun.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ashiʿʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ashiʿʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣawwara aṭ-ṭabīb sāqahu bi-l-ashiʿʿa.} — The doctor X-rayed his leg.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a diagnosis, then the Arabic for a lab test, then say \emph{ashiʿʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{أشعة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}X-rays; rays\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عالج} (ʿālaja)}{عالج (ʿālaja)}]{\ar{عالج} (ʿālaja) — to treat (a patient)}

\label{lesson:AR-C510-alaja}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a lab test, then the Arabic for X-rays.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عالج}}
\textbf{\ar{عالج}} — \emph{ʿālaja} — \textquotedblleft{}to treat (a patient)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{عالجت} \ar{الطبيبة} \ar{الجرح} \ar{بسرعة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ʿālajat aṭ-ṭabība al-jurḥ bi-surʿa.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The doctor treated the wound quickly.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يعالج}, \emph{yuʿālij}.

The noun \ar{علاج}, treatment, goes with it.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عالج}} (\emph{ʿālaja}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-l-j}, \textquotedblleft{}to work at, to struggle with\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form III ʿālaja is to work at a thing until it gives way.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿālaja}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿālaja}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿālajat aṭ-ṭabība al-jurḥ bi-surʿa.} — The doctor treated the wound quickly.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a lab test, then the Arabic for X-rays, then say \emph{ʿālaja} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عالج} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To treat (a patient)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{داوى} (dāwā)}{داوى (dāwā)}]{\ar{داوى} (dāwā) — to cure}

\label{lesson:AR-C510-dawa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for X-rays, then the Arabic for to treat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{داوى}}
\textbf{\ar{داوى}} — \emph{dāwā} — \textquotedblleft{}to cure\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{جدتي} \ar{تداوي} \ar{الناس} \ar{بالأعشاب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat jaddatī tudāwī an-nās bi-l-aʿshāb.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandmother used to cure people with herbs.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يداوي}, \emph{yudāwī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{داوى}} (\emph{dāwā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{d-w-y}, \textquotedblleft{}sickness; a cure\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Dawāʾ, medicine, which you know, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dāwā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dāwā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kānat jaddatī tudāwī an-nās bi-l-aʿshāb.} — My grandmother used to cure people with herbs.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for X-rays, then the Arabic for to treat, then say \emph{dāwā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{داوى} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To cure\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
